title: [PM-40320] feat: Add bulk action support to shared VaultItemsTableComponent
body:
## 🎟️ Tracking

https://bitwarden.atlassian.net/browse/PM-40320

Addresses https://bitwarden.atlassian.net/browse/PM-43237

## 📔 Objective

Gives the shared `VaultItemsTableComponent` bulk-action support: checking rows drives `VaultBatchBarService`'s `can*` permission signals and `bulk*` methods, so `<bit-vault-batch-action>` follows from the selection with **no per-client wiring**.

**The table owns the selection; the bar reads it.** Rather than keeping `bit-table-v2`'s signal-native `TableSelectionModel<C>` in sync with the batch bar's CDK `SelectionModel<VaultItem<C>>`, the table registers a read-only projection of its own model as the bar's selection source. Because the shared table is cipher-only, the projection is the total function `C` → `{ cipher: C }`.

That inversion came out of review — the first version bridged the two models with a pair of effects and `untracked` writes, which meant reconciling ownership, key strategy, and item shape all at once. Registration removes the second model entirely, so the two can't disagree. It also surfaced that desktop's `VaultListTableComponent` was already mirroring selection into the same CDK model, making the bridge a duplicate writer; that manual sync is deleted.

```ts
// VaultBatchBarService
registerSelection(source: VaultSelectionSource<C>): () => void
```

The CDK model stays as the **default** source, so the legacy `vault-items.component` and anything reading `selection` directly are untouched — the service's existing specs drive it through 91 `service.selection.*` calls and pass unchanged. `canRestore` and `canDelete` moved from `selection.changed` to `toObservable(selected)` so they follow a registered source, and every clear path funnels through `clearSelection()`.

`VaultBatchBarService` is injected `{ optional: true }` — a host that doesn't render the bar needn't provide it, and the table is then a plain selectable list.

### Selection cap

Bulk actions turn each selected row into a permission check and a request payload, so select-all is bounded at `MAX_SELECTION_COUNT = 500`, matching the cap the legacy component applies. This is a new `max` option on `TableSelectionConfig` in `libs/components`, defaulting to `Infinity` so existing tables are unaffected.

The cap binds the **selection**, not a downstream view of it — capping the projection instead left rows checked that no action would touch. Consequences, each found in review and each covered by a regression test:

- `allSelected` measures against the capped set, so the header resolves at the cap instead of sticking indeterminate; `indeterminate` measures over the full in-scope set, or a row past the cap window would render checked above an empty header.
- Row checkboxes bind `disabled` to `full()` (excluding selected rows). Left enabled, a rejected click still flips the browser's `checked` property, and since the `[checked]` binding's value never changes Angular never writes it back — the row renders selected when it isn't.
- `toggleAll()` clears when the budget is spent, so a selection at `max` doesn't dead-end when the filter moves off those rows.
- The model scopes over rows in **display order** (a new `sorted` signal, filtered and sorted but not paginated). Scoped over the pre-sort `filtered`, a capped select-all kept 500 rows scattered through the list rather than the 500 the user sees.

Single-select no longer renders a select-all header — `toggleAll` could only ever keep one row, leaving the checkbox permanently indeterminate with no way to clear. Latent rather than user-facing: no current consumer configures `multiple: false`.

### Not included

The web `VaultNextComponent` renders this table but provides neither `VaultBatchBarService` nor `<bit-vault-batch-action>`, so the bar does not appear there yet. Desktop's `vault.component` does both and works today. Wiring web is a separate integration.

There is also no user-facing copy at the cap — a user who selects 500 sees the remaining checkboxes disable with no explanation, as does one whose budget is held by rows a filter has hidden. Both need i18n across four apps plus a placement decision, so they belong with the host that renders them.

### Testing

44 specs added across the model, the service, the table, and the bar. Each regression test was mutation-verified rather than trusted green — reverting the fix it covers makes it fail.

- `libs/vault` — 1315 tests / 76 suites
- `libs/components` + `libs/vault` + desktop vault + web vault — 2144 tests / 158 suites
- `tsc` clean for both libs; lint and prettier clean

### Storybook

Stories use the real `VaultBatchBarService` subclassed to report actions to the Actions panel rather than opening dialogs. Previously they provided the real service outright, so triggering Archive or Move opened a CDK dialog whose component was never imported and left a bare overlay over the page. That also surfaced seven i18n keys the row copy menu needs but the stories never mocked — `I18nMockService` throws on an unmocked key, which killed change detection mid-render, so the bar never appeared at all.

`bit-vault-batch-action` portals into `LayoutFooterService` and renders nothing without a `bit-layout`, so a minimal story-only outlet stands in — wrapping every story in the full layout would bury the table in navigation chrome. The same outlet is now reused in the bar's spec, replacing an assertion that matched raw template text.

A `SelectableCapped` story in `table-v2.stories.ts` demonstrates the cap at `max: 3` over 5 rows, since 500 isn't observable in a viewport.

## 📸 Screenshots

Checking rows shows the bar with the permission-gated actions; **Clear** unchecks every row and dismisses it. At the cap, select-all stops short, the header still resolves as checked, and the remaining checkboxes disable.

🎨 Having to keep two sources of truth for the selection in sync (BatchBarService and TableV2's internal selection) seems like quite the headache after seeing it written out. Perhaps we can considering consolidating the selection model source into one place? Below is some ideating I did with Claude that may be helpful (feel free to ignore if you feel differently).

<details>
<summary> 🤖 Brainstorm  </summary>
Let the service read the table's selection instead of syncing two models

The `bridgeSelection` / `syncFromBatchBar` pair works, but it reconciles ownership, key strategy (row reference vs cipher id), and item shape all at once — and `syncFromBatchBar` has to infer intent, reading "bar is empty" as "bar asked us to clear."

Worth considering inverting it. The service's own use of its model is narrow — it reads selected/changed and calls `clear()`, never select/deselect/toggle/setSelection — so the contract is two members:

```ts
export interface VaultSelectionSource<C extends CipherViewLike> {
  readonly selected: Signal<readonly VaultItem<C>[]>;
  clear(): void;
}
```

`VaultBatchBarService` keeps its CDK model as a default source and gains `registerSelection(source)` returning a teardown. That default is what makes it non-breaking: the legacy vault list needs no change (its ~30 call sites go through one get selection()), and `vault-batch-bar.service.spec.ts` needs none either.

The table then registers a pure computed projection of `TableSelectionModel` and deregisters via `DestroyRef`. Both `effects` and both `untracked()` calls go away, and because the bar reads a projection rather than holding a copy it can't report a selection the checkboxes don't show. It also closes the destroy leak (service is provided above the table, so a stale selection currently outlives it) and gives one choke point for a select-all cap — the component this replaces caps at `MaxSelectionCount = 500`.
</details>

🎨 It may be helpful to have the storybook extend this service so that it can fire the storybook `action()` hooks whenever a batch bar action is "performed". Currently, the real service attempts to open the dialog and bricks the story. (It looks like just the dialog overlay fires, because the actual dialogs aren't imported/necessary for this story).

❌ **CRITICAL**: The web host on this PR's base renders this table without providing `VaultBatchBarService`, so the vault route will throw `NullInjectorError`.

<details>
<summary>Details and fix</summary>

The PR description notes "No consumer exists on this base" — that held while this was stacked on `vault/pm-40312/...`, but the base is now `main` and PM-40312 has landed, so a consumer does exist:

- `apps/web/src/app/vault/individual-vault/vault-next.component.html:8` renders `<vault-items-table>`
- `apps/web/src/app/vault/individual-vault/vault-next.component.ts:75-78` provides only `DefaultCipherFormConfigService` and `WebVaultItemActionsService`

`VaultBatchBarService` is `@Injectable()` with no `providedIn`, and nothing in the ancestor chain provides it — `vault.module.ts` and `vault-routing.module.ts` declare no providers, and the only web providers are the legacy `individual-vault/vault.component.ts:186` and `admin-console/organizations/collections/vault.component.ts:141`, neither of which is an ancestor of `VaultNextComponent` (it is a top-level route component). With `FeatureFlag.VFO1Foundation` on, constructing the table throws `NG0201: No provider for VaultBatchBarService` and the page fails to render.

CI will not catch this: `vault-next.component.spec.ts:201-211` replaces the table with `NO_ERRORS_SCHEMA`.

Desktop is unaffected — `apps/desktop/src/vault/app/vault-v3/vault.component.ts:163` provides the service above `app-vault-list-table`.

Two ways out:

1. Wire the host in this PR — provide `VaultBatchBarService` in `VaultNextComponent` along with the collaborators it injects that are not root-provided (`RoutedVaultFilterService`, `RoutedVaultFilterBridgeService`, `ASSIGN_COLLECTIONS_DIALOG`, `BULK_DELETE_DIALOG`), and render `<bit-vault-batch-action />` as the class docs now require.
2. Inject with `{ optional: true }` and no-op both effects when it is absent, so a host without a batch bar keeps working.
</details>

♻️ **DEBT**: The desktop host now writes the same selection a second time, since it still bridges via `(selectedChange)`.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

`apps/desktop/src/vault/app/vault-v3/vault-list-table/vault-list-table.component.html:20` binds `(selectedChange)="handleSelectionChange($event)"`, and that handler (`vault-list-table.component.ts:72-78`) does `selection.clear()` then `selection.select(...)` on the *same* `VaultBatchBarService` instance this effect writes to — the service is provided once at `vault-v3/vault.component.ts:163`.

Worth deleting `handleSelectionChange` (and its `{ optional: true }` injection, which is moot now that the table requires the service) here or in an immediate follow-up.

Agreed — writing the bridge out made the same thing obvious to me. Done in e85193687c.

Two things I found while implementing that make the case stronger than the design argument alone:

**Desktop already had a competing bridge.** `vault-list-table.component.ts` wired `(selectedChange)` → `selection.clear()` + `select(...)`, so this PR wasn't just keeping two models in sync — it added a *second* writer to the same CDK model on that host. Both fired on every selection change. That's deleted now.

**The required inject was breaking.** Desktop injects `VaultBatchBarService` with `{ optional: true }`; I'd made it required in the shared table, so any host not providing it would throw NullInjectorError. Now optional.

One wrinkle worth noting since it wasn't in the sketch: `canRestore` and `canDelete` were keyed on `this.selection.changed` — the Observable, not `selected()` — so they'd have ignored a registered source entirely. Both moved to `toObservable(this.selected)`. Same for `bulkDelete`, which read `this.selection.selected` directly and would have acted on the CDK model rather than the source.

Shape is as you described: `registerSelection(source)` taking `{ selected, clear }`, CDK model kept as the default source so the legacy vault-items component and the existing service specs are untouched, table registers a computed projection and deregisters via the effect's `onCleanup` (which closes the destroy leak). Both effects and both `untracked()` calls are gone. Also folded in the `MAX_SELECTION_COUNT = 500` cap since it's now a single choke point.

I left the legacy web `vault-items.component` on the default source — migrating it would let us drop its local `MaxSelectionCount` and `_localSelection`, but that felt like a separate PR.

❌ **CRITICAL**: The bar's own Clear button no-ops once a selection source is registered.

<details>
<summary>Details and fix</summary>

`vault-batch-action.component.html:9` binds `(clear)="service.selection.clear()"` — the CDK model, not this new `clearSelection()`. With a source registered, `selected()` returns `source()?.selected()` and never consults `defaultSelection()`, so clearing the CDK model changes nothing observable: `selectedCount()` is unchanged, the bar stays up, and every row stays checked.

Desktop hits this as soon as both flags are on — `apps/desktop/src/vault/app/vault-v3/vault.component.html:22` renders `app-vault-list-table` (which wraps the shared `vault-items-table`, now registering a source) and line 67 renders `<bit-vault-batch-action />` against the same provided service instance.

Every other clear path already routes correctly (`completed$`, route-filter changes, each `bulk*`), so only the button is affected.

Fix: make `clearSelection()` public and bind the bar to it.

```html
<bit-bulk-actions-bar [selectedCount]="service.selectedCount()" (clear)="service.clearSelection()">
```

</details>

⚠️ **IMPORTANT**: Capping the projection rather than the selection leaves rows checked that the bar will never act on.

<details>
<summary>Details and fix</summary>

`TableSelectionModel.toggleAll()` selects every selectable filtered row with no cap (`table-selection-model.ts:108`), so over 500 rows the header and all row checkboxes read as selected while the bar reports 500. A bulk delete then deletes 500, `clearSelection()` unchecks everything, and the remaining rows are silently left behind with no error.

The legacy component this mirrors avoids the divergence by capping the *selection*, not a downstream view of it — `vault-items.component.ts:421` selects `sortedItems.slice(0, MaxSelectionCount)` and `isAllSelected` (line 312) measures over the same 500, so the checkbox state always equals the acted-on set.

Two ways to restore that invariant:

1. Drop the cap here so the bar and the checkboxes agree, and enforce a limit where select-all happens instead.
2. Add a max to `TableSelectionConfig` / `TableSelectionModel` so `toggleAll()` stops at the cap and the UI reflects what will be acted on.

</details>

Good catch — fixed in ad183c328a.

You were right about the cause: the story stubs the two *token*-based dialogs (`ASSIGN_COLLECTIONS_DIALOG`, `BULK_DELETE_DIALOG`), but `DialogService` itself was never provided, so `bulkArchive` (`openSimpleDialog`) and `bulkMoveToFolder` (`openBulkMoveDialog`) hit the real CDK dialog with no component imported — hence the bare overlay. `bulkUnarchive`/`bulkRestore` would have gone to the server too, just less visibly.

Went with subclassing as you suggested rather than faking the service: the selection source and the `can*` signals are what the stories actually demonstrate, so `StoryVaultBatchBarService` overrides only the seven action bodies. Each reports to the Actions panel with the items it would have applied to, then clears the selection so the bar dismisses like a completed action would. `clearSelection()` became `protected` so it clears through the table's registered source rather than the now-unused default CDK model.

Verified in Storybook — Archive and Delete both come back with 0 overlay panes, 0 backdrops, selection cleared, and one entry in the Actions panel.

Separately, while verifying I hit a pre-existing bug that was blocking this: the row copy menu asks for seven i18n keys the story never mocked (`copy`, `noDetailsToCopy`, and the five `no*` fallbacks). `I18nMockService` throws on an unmocked key, which killed change detection mid-render — so the batch bar never appeared at all once a row was checked. Added in 40c4178539.

inline.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT**: Once the selection is at `max`, select-all becomes an inert checkbox if the filter moves off the selected rows.

<details>
<summary>Trace and fix</summary>

With `max: 500` over 1200 rows:

1. Select-all takes rows 0–499. `allSelected()` is true, header checked.
2. Narrow the filter (search term, type chip) to a set that excludes those rows. `filtered` changes, so `selectableWithinMax()` is now the new set with none of it selected → `allSelected()` false **and** `indeterminate()` false. The header renders unchecked.
3. Clicking it calls `toggleAll()` → not all selected → `select(...selectableWithinMax())` → the loop breaks on the first iteration because `next.length` is already 500. Nothing is selected, the binding snaps the checkbox back to unchecked, and there is no way to select in this filtered view without clearing first.

The legacy `vault-items.component` doesn't dead-end here because it caps only the select-all batch (`sortedItems.slice(0, MaxSelectionCount)`) while its CDK model has no ceiling, so a second select-all still adds rows.

One option is to treat a full budget as "all selected", so the click clears rather than no-ops:

```ts
readonly allSelected = computed(() => {
  const rows = this.selectableWithinMax();
  return rows.length > 0 && (this.count() >= this.max || rows.every((row) => this.isSelected(row)));
});
```

That trades one oddity for another (the header reads checked while the visible rows aren't), so having `toggleAll()` clear when `count() >= max` may read better — either way the checkbox stays actionable.
</details>

⚠️ **IMPORTANT**: At the cap, a rejected row click leaves the checkbox rendered as checked while the row is not selected.

<details>
<summary>Details and fix</summary>

`toggle(row)` → `select(row)`; once `count() === max` the loop breaks immediately, so `isSelected(row)` is `false` before and after the click.

The click has already flipped the native `checked` property on the DOM node. `table-v2.component.html` binds `[checked]="sel.isSelected(row)"`, and Angular only writes a property binding when the bound value *changes* — it was `false` and is still `false`, so nothing rewrites it. The box stays visually checked. `bit-row` compounds it: `has-[[data-selection-input]:checked]:tw-bg-bg-brand-soft` keys off the DOM `:checked` state, so the whole row renders highlighted too.

That is the exact failure this cap was added to prevent — a row that looks selected but that no bulk action will touch. With 500 already selected in a large vault, a user checking a 501st row and hitting Delete gets it silently skipped.

Suggested fix — make the click impossible rather than inert:

```ts
/** Whether the cap is reached, so no further row may be selected. */
readonly full = computed(() => this.count() >= this.max);
```

and in `table-v2.component.html`:

```html
<input
  bitCheckbox
  type="checkbox"
  slot="start"
  data-selection-input
  [attr.aria-label]="'selectRow' | i18n"
  [checked]="sel.isSelected(row)"
  [disabled]="sel.full() && !sel.isSelected(row)"
  (change)="sel.toggle(row)"
/>
```

This also communicates the limit to the user instead of the checkbox appearing to work.

</details>

⚠️ **IMPORTANT**: After a capped select-all, the header checkbox renders checked with nothing selected — `[checked]` is never written back.

<details>
<summary>Trace and fix</summary>

With a `max` set, a select-all click leaves `allSelected()` false, because it measures the full `selectable()` set (`table-selection-model.spec.ts:122` pins that: "reads as partial at the cap, not complete"). So:

1. Click select-all over 600 rows with `max: 500`. The browser sets the input's `checked` property to `true`. `[checked]="sel.allSelected()"` was `false` and still is, so Angular skips the write — the DOM property stays `true`, masked only because `[indeterminate]` flips `false → true`.
2. Anything that makes `indeterminate()` false while `allSelected()` stays false unmasks it. The bar's Clear button is the shortest path: `clearSelection()` → `model.clear()` → `indeterminate` `true → false` (written), `allSelected` `false → false` (not written). The header then renders as fully checked with zero rows selected and the bar dismissed. Narrowing a filter off the selected rows does the same, as does `toggleAll()`'s new clear-at-cap branch when the filter has moved off the selection.

`bitCheckbox` cannot correct it either — its own `[checked]` host binding reads `isGroupChecked()`, which has no signal dependency in the standalone path and so is evaluated once and frozen.

This is the same mechanism as the row-checkbox divergence fixed in `31b2c090bf`; that one was closed with `[disabled]`, which the header has no equivalent for. Restoring the DOM state after the toggle is the smallest fix:

```ts
/**
 * `toggleAll()` can leave `allSelected()` unchanged (a capped select-all, or a clear at the cap),
 * and Angular skips an unchanged `[checked]` write — so restore what the model implies.
 */
protected toggleAllRows(model: TableSelectionModel<T>, input: HTMLInputElement): void {
  model.toggleAll();
  input.checked = model.allSelected();
}
```

```html
(change)="toggleAllRows(sel, $any($event.target))"
```

Only capped tables are affected, so today that is the vault table with more than `MAX_SELECTION_COUNT` items in scope.
</details>
